customer_acme: Hey team, embedding endpoint started failing for us after we switched to batching. Getting 400s and some 422s. Payload example: we send a list of vectors. Any idea?

alex (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact request body and the error text from the response?

customer_acme: Sure, here's the request we send from our worker (Node):

```json
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"model\": \"open-embed-xxl\",
  \"input\": [[[0.12,0.03, ... , 0.01]]]  // we build vectors client-side and batch them
}
```

And the server responds: `400 Bad Request` with body: `{ \"error\": \"Invalid input shape: expected array of strings or array of vectors, got nested-array depth 3\" }`. Sometimes we also see: `422 Unprocessable Entity - embedding dimension mismatch (1535 vs 1536)`.

alex (Support): OK that helps. Two quick things: 1) our embeddings API accepts either an array of strings (to embed text) or an array of vectors (numeric arrays) but vectors must be 1D arrays representing each embedding, and the top-level must be an array of those vectors (so depth 2). Your example has an extra wrapping-level (depth 3). 2) The 1535 vs 1536 message means one of the vectors was the wrong length — often caused by flattening mistakes or trailing punctuation removal in a pre-processing step.

sam (SDK): Adding: the JS SDK will auto-batch if you pass multiple inputs as an array of strings/vectors. If you pre-batch at the transport layer (e.g., send a single array-of-arrays-of-arrays), the server interprets that as a single item containing nested arrays which trips validation. Example correct shapes below.

sam (SDK): Correct (text):
```json
{ \"model\": \"open-embed-xxl\", \"input\": [\"hello world\", \"how are you?\"] }
```
Correct (vectors):
```json
{ \"model\": \"open-embed-xxl\", \"input\": [[0.12, 0.03, ... , 0.01], [0.08, 0.99, ... , 0.11]] }
```
Incorrect (double-wrapped):
```json
{ \"model\": \"open-embed-xxl\", \"input\": [[[0.12, ...]]] }
```

customer_acme: Ahhh, we do double-wrap in our worker because we thought we had to group batches per-request. We also have a fallback that retries with a smaller batch size when we see errors — could that explain a billing jump?

alex (Support): Yes, the retry loop can multiply billable requests. If your retry fires N times for a batch of M items, you may incur N*M requests billed. Also some clients will re-send the same vectors multiple times. We can check call logs to confirm.

kevin (Eng-ML): Quick note on the dimension mismatch: one common pattern is converting text -> token vectors in the client and then post-processing (slicing/truncation) that inadvertently removes a value from one vector. If you compute length with something like `arr.length - 1` in a reduce, one item can become 1535. We see this with custom quantization tools too.

customer_acme: Attached our minimal repro below (Python). We take a batch of raw vectors and call requests.post(json=payload).

```python
# BAD: double-wrapped
payload = {\"model\":\"open-embed-xxl\",\"input\":[[vec1, vec2]]}
requests.post(url, json=payload)

# GOOD
payload = {\"model\":\"open-embed-xxl\",\"input\":[vec1, vec2]}
requests.post(url, json=payload)
```

alex (Support): Thanks, this is great. Can you do two quick experiments and paste the responses?
1) Send a single vector correctly-shaped to confirm the model and dimension (expect 200).
2) Send two vectors as an array (no extra nesting).

customer_acme: Running test 1 now... got 200 and the embedding length is 1536. Test 2 also 200. When we run their worker in prod with the double-wrap we hit ~15% 400s and the retry loop triggered ~3x, so we got charged for ~45% extra requests.

alex (Support): Oof. We'll do two things: I'll open a billing alert ticket to investigate the overcharge (cc @billing-bot) and sam/kevin can follow up on SDK guidance and validation. For immediate mitigation, please:
- Stop the auto-retry or add dedupe on the request ID
- Fix the worker batching to use the correct top-level input array

sam (SDK): I'll add a client-side validation helper that detects nested-array depths > 2 and raises before sending. Example: `validateEmbeddingsPayload(payload)` that checks `Array.isArray(payload.input) && !Array.isArray(payload.input[0][0])` etc. I'll follow up with a small patch and publish a note in the SDK changelog.

kevin (Eng-ML): I can also add a defensive server-side error message that points to double-wrapping and includes the offending item's index and shape to speed up debugging. I'll open an internal PR.

billing-bot: Billing ticket created: BT-4891. Suspended auto-charge review for customer_acme pending investigation.

customer_acme: Thanks everyone — implemented the quick fix (unwrapped the input) and disabled retries. Error rate dropped to ~0.5%. Can you confirm billing follow-up?

alex (Support): Confirmed BT-4891 is assigned to finance; they will review the spike and follow up in 48 hours. Closing this thread unless anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

customer_acme: All good. Appreciate the quick help. :heart:
